scope: Reviewed authored English directions only. No student data.

records.text: What you will make. At the wind model. Moving air turns the blades and generator. We will make the board show its voltage, then compare fan-off and fan-on readings. Voltage is electrical push, measured in volts, written V. Use the already-built wind model. Keep the generator disconnected from the Ardweeno until its input circuit is checked. Check. The blades turn the generator. A meter reading in V shows measured voltage; spinning alone does not.

Check the board and parts. At the Freenove board. The photo shows the Freenove Projects Board V1.2 used for these directions. It does not show the wiring of your turbine prototype. The smaller control board plugs into it. Find the Freenove Projects Board V1.2, its control board, U S B data cable, multimeter, AA holder, breadboard, wires and two ten kilohm resistors. Check. Your teacher confirms a classic Uno-compatible 5 V control board and checks both ten kilohm resistor values. The turbine stays disconnected.

Set the board switches. At the Freenove board. The number display is already wired inside the board. Some other modules share its pins or A zero, so we must turn those modules off. Disconnect U S B and every signal source. Set Digital Tube, module 15, ON. Set all unused modules OFF, including Light Res and Thermistor. Check. The board is unpowered. Digital Tube is ON, and the two A zero sensor switches are OFF.

Open the display check. In this guide. Test the existing display before connecting a measuring signal. This small sketch should show zero one two three. A sketch is an Ardweeno program. Download DisplayCheck.ino and open it in Ardweeno I D E. Check. The editor shows the supplied display-check sketch. No generator or battery is connected.

Connect U S B and choose the board. In Ardweeno I D E. A U S B data cable carries the program from the computer. The board choice must match the actual plugged-in control board. Connect the U S B data cable. In Ardweeno I D E, select the teacher-confirmed Ardweeno Uno board and its U S B port. Check. Ardweeno I D E shows the checked board and a connected port.

Upload and check zero one two three. In Ardweeno I D E. Upload copies the program to the connected board. U S B supplies board power. There is still no measuring source connected. Click Upload. When it finishes, check that all four display positions read zero one two three in order. Check. All four digits are readable and correctly ordered. Stop here if any digit is wrong or missing.

Open the voltage program. In this guide. WindVoltageBench.ino is a supplied bench-test program. You will read its main parts instead of typing a long program without understanding it. Download WindVoltageBench.ino and open it in Ardweeno I D E. Keep the generator disconnected. Check. The complete voltage sketch is visible. Keep a copy of the downloaded file.

Find the input and display pins. In Ardweeno I D E. A zero turns the voltage into a number from 0 to one thousand twenty three on this checked board. D eleven sends display patterns, D thirteen moves their bits and D twelve makes the pattern appear. The display wires are already on the board. Find these four pin names near the top of the sketch. Keep their supplied values. Check. VOLTAGE_PIN is A zero. Display data is D eleven, clock D thirteen and latch D twelve.

See how the count becomes volts. In Ardweeno I D E. The code averages eight A zero samples. The two equal ten kilohm resistors halve the source voltage, so input scale is 2 to scale the estimate back up. Find this line in readVoltage. Follow it from left to right. Check. total / 8.0 finds the average count. * means multiply and / means divide. The rest converts that count into an estimate of source volts.

See how the display stays readable. In Ardweeno I D E. The program rounds the voltage to hundredths and shows whole volts, tenths and hundredths. It lights each digit briefly, over and over, so all digits look steady. Find makeScreen and the four-position scan in loop. Keep the supplied DIGIT table and sendDigit function. Check. The decimal point follows the first digit. The fourth position is blank. Avoid long pauses in the display loop.

Know when to stop. In Ardweeno I D E. zero point zero zero means near zero, but does not prove a source is connected. four dashes is a software warning, not electrical protection. Unsafe voltage can damage A zero before the program reacts. Before applying any signal, find the dashes condition shown here. If dashes appear during a test, have your teacher remove the input signal and check the circuit. Check. You will stop on dashes. You will not treat zero point zero zero as proof that a source is connected.

Wire the known AA test circuit. At the Freenove board. This bench circuit uses two equal ten kilohm resistors. A zero connects between them and sees about half the known AA voltage. This drawing is not final turbine wiring. Disconnect U S B and the AA source. Place the two ten kilohm resistors as drawn. Join their middle point to A zero and their lower end to board ground. Leave the AA source disconnected. Check. The teacher checks the connected breadboard rows, both resistor values, A zero at the midpoint and the shared ground before power is applied.

Run the voltage program. In Ardweeno I D E. The complete supplied sketch handles measuring and display refresh together. After the wiring check, connect U S B and upload WindVoltageBench.ino. Open Serial Monitor at ninety six hundred baud. Check. Upload finishes. Serial Monitor shows Voltage and A D C lines.

Check zero before the battery. At the Freenove board. With no source connected, the lower resistor holds A zero near ground. This gives a useful first check. With the AA source disconnected, read the display and Serial Monitor. Check. Both should show a near-zero estimate, about zero point zero zero V.

Compare with a known voltage. At the Freenove board. A known source lets us check the estimate before using the generator. The meter must measure across the AA terminals, not just A zero to ground. With divider wiring checked and U S B power on, have your teacher apply the AA signal through the prepared connections: positive through the upper resistor, negative to ground. Compare the display with the checked meter across the AA terminals. Check. The teacher records the difference and checks whether calibration is adequate. Remove the AA signal before removing U S B power.

Set up the generator-only meter test. At the stationary generator · teacher checks the clips. The generator voltage is still unknown. A red LED lighting does not establish its maximum. Keep the Ardweeno completely disconnected for this check. With fan off and blades stopped, have your teacher identify the output type and choose its voltage mode and range. Check black in COM and red in V. Attach one probe to each generator terminal. Check. The Ardweeno and intentional loads are disconnected. Clips are clear of blades. Never use current mode across the generator.

Measure the generator on its own. At the Freenove board. The interface must suit the generator over the intended test conditions. One slow test is not enough. A meter can still miss fast spikes. Have your teacher test the intended fan settings and distances, including the highest intended speed. Record the maximum observed voltage, polarity and output type. Check. The record contains real meter readings. A minus sign is recorded, not ignored.

Check the protected generator interface. At the Freenove board. An interface is the circuit between the generator and A zero. Its divider, load and protection depend on the measured voltage, polarity and possible spikes. The final design still needs a physical teacher check. Continue only after your teacher physically tests and approves the actual circuit between the generator and A zero. If it is not approved, save the bench work and stop here. Check. The interface handles the measured range, polarity and possible spikes. A zero stays nonnegative and below the powered reference voltage.

Match the code to the checked circuit. In Ardweeno I D E. The bench sketch assumes two ten kilohm resistors. A different final divider needs its actual resistor values in the sketch. Its calibration must match the real board. Have your teacher enter the actual resistor values and reference voltage. Save as WindVoltage_Checked_01 and upload with the generator signal disconnected. Check. The saved sketch matches the approved interface and calibration.

Check the live generator display. At the Freenove board. All wiring changes happen with power and signal removed. The board must then have U S B power before a generator signal is present. Have your teacher connect the approved interface with power and signal removed, power the board by U S B, then apply the generator signal. Compare meter and display at the same source terminals under the same load. Check. The teacher checks fan-off/on readings at the same loaded terminals. Record the approved interface and calibration. At shutdown, remove the generator signal before removing U S B power.

Set up a fair comparison. In the team test record. A fair comparison changes the fan condition while keeping the other parts the same. Your teacher chooses a safe position and one fan-on setting. Open your team test record. Record the marked fan distance in centimetres, fan-on setting, settling time and wait between readings. Write your expected voltage change and reason. Check. Use the checked multimeter for recorded readings and compare the Ardweeno display alongside it. The teacher checks the complete setup before testing.

Take three fan-off readings. At the model and in the team test record. Three readings help you see whether the number stays steady. A real zero is a result; a missing reading is not zero. With fan off and blades stopped, take three multimeter readings using the agreed wait. Under Before change, fan off, record readings 1, 2 and 3, each with V. Compare the Ardweeno display too. Check. Your test record has three real fan-off readings, including decimal points and any minus signs.

Take three fan-on readings. At the model and in the team test record. Keep the marked distance, fan setting, connections and wait unchanged. Have your teacher start the guarded fan. After the settling time, record three multimeter readings under Before change, fan on. Compare the Ardweeno display. Then stop the fan and wait for all blades to stop. Check. Your original record now has six readings, three off and three on.

Compare and choose one improvement. In the team report. Compare the three fan-off readings with the three fan-on readings. Look for higher, lower, similar or changing readings. You do not need to calculate an average. Compare the three off readings with the three on readings. Use actual values to describe the pattern. Choose one small change with your teacher and record why the evidence supports it. Check. Your report says whether the pattern matched your prediction and names just one approved change.

Make the change and repeat the test. At the wind model. Changing just one thing makes the comparison easier to explain. Keep the first results. With fan off and blades stopped, make the approved change with your teacher and record its date. After the setup check, repeat three multimeter readings off and three on under After change. Compare the Ardweeno display and stop the fan afterward. Check. Both sets of six readings are saved. Use the same distance, fan setting and timing unless that was the one approved change.

Explain what the results show. In the team report. Use both sets of real results. A change may help, make no clear difference or make the result worse. All three findings are useful. Under Test and improvement, compare actual before/after voltages. Say whether the change helped, made no clear difference or made the result worse. State one limit. Check. Your explanation uses real values and says this test measured voltage under the recorded conditions.

Save your test evidence. In the team Drive folder. Keep the checked Ardweeno program, original and after-change test records, and current team report together. The blank CSV is a backup for recording tests, not completed evidence. Save the actual program, test record and report in the team Drive folder. Check. The folder contains the checked sketch and the real evidence, including any test marked Test not run.
